trim: Stingray Coupe with Z51 Performance Package (6.2L LT2 V8, 495 hp with the Z51's performance exhaust, 8-speed dual-clutch, RWD)

fields.text: 6.2-liter LT2 pushrod V8 with direct fuel injection
fields.note: Carried over from the earlier card research (2026-11-11): a search summary described the LT2 in the 2024 Stingray as a 6.2-liter pushrod V8, and a second result said it uses direct fuel injection. The wording is the reference site's; no maker page surfaced. The card reviewer confirmed LT2 / 6.2 L / V8 but did not see 'pushrod' or 'direct injection' again. Same engine in every Stingray trim, Z51 included. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

fields.note: A search summary quoted Corvette Magazine's 'Two Clutches, No Waiting' article on the C8's Tremec 8-speed DCT: 'Gear ratios are 2.91, 1.76, 1.22, 0.88, 0.65, 0.51, 0.40, and 0.33:1, providing a total spread of 8.82:1 over the eight cogs', with reverse 2.63:1. Hagerty's piece on the Tremec TR-9080 names the same 0.33:1 eighth gear. An earlier summary listed the same first six ratios from 2020 Chevrolet material. Written for the 2020 launch; the 2024 Stingray uses the same 8-speed DCT (see transmissionType). The Z51 changes the final drive, not these ratios, as far as any result said. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

fields.publisher: Chevrolet (press release republished by National Corvette Museum)
fields.note: A search summary quoted Chevrolet's 2020 material, republished by the National Corvette Museum: 'An electronic limited slip differential is offered on the Z51 Performance Package and has an effective final drive ratio of 5.2:1', with the table 'eLSD | 5.2:1 | 1.46 | 3.55:1' (effective final drive | transfer gear ratio | ring and pinion ratio); the base car's mechanical LSD is 4.9:1 (1.38 transfer gear, same 3.55:1 ring and pinion). This is the overall ratio after the transaxle's transfer gear, i.e. multiply each gear ratio by 5.2 (1.46 x 3.55). Owner-forum posts give the Z51 as 5.17 and the base car as 4.89 (see conflicts). 2020 model-year material; the 2024 Z51 package was described as still including a 'performance rear axle ratio'. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.
fields.checkNote: The Chevrolet table republished by the National Corvette Museum pairs the eLSD with 5.2:1 (1.46 transfer gear, 3.55:1 ring and pinion), and forum posts quoting Chevrolet give 5.17 (one 5.18) for Z51 cars, the same gearing to more places.

fields.publisher: Chevrolet (press release republished by National Corvette Museum)

fields.checkNote: Tremec's specification lists a mechanical limited-slip differential as standard and an electronic one as optional, and the Chevrolet table ties the eLSD to the 5.2:1 ratio that forum posts give for Z51 cars.

fields.publisher: Car and Driver (syndicated on Yahoo Autos)
fields.note: Same Yahoo Autos report of Car and Driver's scale test: the split is 39.4/60.6 front/rear for the 2020 Z51 coupe (versus roughly 49.4/50.1 for the C7). A separate summary of MotorTrend's test said 61 percent of the weight sits on the rear tires. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.
fields.checkNote: The scale-test results that surfaced again gave the 3,647 lb weight but not the front/rear split; only a rounded 40/60 pre-production figure appeared.

conflicts.note: Not recorded. Listings disagree and none names the Z51 package: 3,535 lb (Edmunds and Motor Matchup, 2024 Stingray coupe 2LT); 3,467 lb 'base curb weight' (cars.com, trim unclear); 3,637 / 3,669 / 3,769 lb (iSeeCars, 2024 trims, 3,769 for the 3LT coupe); 3,366 lb is a 'dry weight' on CorvSport's 2020 specification page. 3,647 lb is Car and Driver's scale weight of a 2020 Z51 coupe, recorded as testWeightLb, and 3,665 lb its 2021 long-term Z51 car. No maker curb weight for the 2024 Z51 coupe surfaced. Second reader (2026-11-24): a further search again found 3,535 lb (Motor Matchup and Edmunds, 2024 coupe), a 3,500 lb 'base curb weight' on a cars.com 2024 listing, and unverified CorvetteForum posts citing 3,538 lb for a Z51 coupe on corner scales and 3,613 lb for a 3LT Z51 'from EPA testing'; Wikipedia gives 3,647-3,913 lb across C8 variants. Still no maker curb weight naming the Z51 coupe, so it stays unrecorded. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Kept 184 mph: Chevrolet's statement (as reported by Yahoo Autos, 2020 model year) that the Z51 car's top speed is 184 mph against 194 mph for the base car, the drop put down to the Z51 aero. Chevrolet's 2024 pages show 194 mph for the Stingray without naming Z51 (Chevrolet Arabia's 2024 page: 312 km/h). Carscoops' 189 mph (304 km/h) had no configuration stated. CorvetteForum reported an independent C8 Z51 run at 191.7 mph, configuration and conditions not given in the summary; not used. topSpeedGoverned remains unsourced. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Kept 2.8 s, Car and Driver's 2020 Z51 coupe test, which also gives the quarter mile, 70-0, skidpad and scale weight. MotorTrend also recorded 2.8 s with an 11.1 s quarter mile at 123.2 mph (as cited by HotCars and Magzter); Car and Driver has more figures for this configuration, so it was kept. Car and Driver's 2021 long-term Z51 car recorded 2.9 s, 11.2 s at 122 mph and 3,665 lb. 2.9 s is also GM's claim for the Z51 car and 3.0 s GM's claim for the base car; neither is a test. Fox News said MotorTrend, Road & Track and Car and Driver all recorded 2.8 s. Second reader (2026-11-24): Edmunds recorded 3.2 s and an 11.5 s quarter mile at more than 120 mph for its own 2020 Z51 test car (a different tester and procedure), and Chevrolet's own table gives 2.9 s and 11.2 s at 121 mph for the Z51. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Kept 495 hp / 470 lb-ft, the rating with the performance exhaust included in Z51. The base Stingray without that exhaust is rated 490 hp / 465 lb-ft. This is a configuration difference, not a disagreement between sources. Second reader (2026-11-24): Motor Matchup's 2024 Stingray 2LT convertible listing shows 490 hp / 465 lb-ft, the base rating. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Kept 5.3 in (Autoblog / iSeeCars, 2024 coupe by trim, Z51 not stated), marked unconfirmed. cars.com shows 5 in for a 2024 convertible, and carsales.com.au shows 100 mm (3.9 in is that figure converted, shown only to mark the disagreement). Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Kept 149 ft (Car and Driver Z51 coupe, retold by MotorBiscuit). Earlier card research saw 148 ft for Car and Driver's 2021 long-term Z51 car and 154 ft is the convertible. An Edmunds result mentioned 105 ft from 60 mph for a Z51 car of unclear model year; MotorTrend's 104 ft 60-0 belongs to the 2014 C7 Z51, not this car. No 60-0 figure for the C8 Z51 surfaced. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Kept 13.6 in (Jalopnik on the Z51 package; a dealer listing gives 13.6 in / 345 mm). Earlier card research saw 13.3 in (345 mm) with Z51 and 12.6 in (321 mm) base on a 2022 CorvSport listing; 345 mm is 13.6 in, so 13.3 looks like a conversion slip on that listing. Corvette Story's 2024 page shows 398 x 38 mm front / 391 x 34 mm rear, which looks like Z06 carbon-ceramic hardware. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Kept Car and Driver's 11.2 s at 122 mph (2020 Z51 coupe; the 2021 long-term car matched it). MotorTrend's C8 Z51 test gave 11.1 s at 123.2 mph (HotCars / Magzter summaries). Different tester and test conditions; not a disagreement about the car. Second reader (2026-11-24): Edmunds recorded 11.5 s at more than 120 mph for its own 2020 Z51 test car (different tester), and Chevrolet's own Z51 claim is 11.2 s at 121 mph. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Kept 62.4 in (1,586 mm, Corvette Story 2024). carsales.com.au gives 1,590 mm (62.6 in, converted only to show the gap) for the 2024 Stingray 2LT and Autopadre's 3LT listing a rounded 62 in. All reference sources; none names Z51. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Kept 5.2:1, Chevrolet's stated effective final drive for the Z51 eLSD (1.46 transfer gear x 3.55 ring and pinion). Owner-forum posts give 5.17 for the Z51 and 4.89 for the base car, which is the same gearing quoted to more places; one forum thread also noted that some leaked C8 final-drive numbers differed from Chevrolet's. Second reader (2026-11-24): Tremec's TR-9080 specification repeats 5.2:1 for the eLSD and 4.9:1 for the mLSD, and one forum post gives 5.18 for the Z51. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Kept 15.7:1 (spec database, likely Corvette Story 2024, variable-ratio rack). A cars.com 2024 trim listing gives an overall steering ratio of 16. Both reference; the rack is variable-ratio. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Kept 6,500 rpm, added by the second reader (2026-11-24) from Motor Matchup's 2024 Stingray coupe 2LT listing and flagged unconfirmed; the first research also saw 6,500 rpm on a result for the 2022 LT2. MotorBiscuit lists the C8 Stingray's redline as 6,450 rpm, which is the power peak rather than a stated rev limit. Neither is a maker figure. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Kept 0.322 for the Z51 car (forum post quoting a Chevrolet aerodynamics engineer). A separate forum post gives 0.32 for the non-Z51 C8. C7 figures (0.30 base, about 0.35 for the C7 Z51, lift 0.20 and about 0.03) were quoted but belong to the previous generation and are not used; no C8 lift coefficient surfaced. Second reader (2026-11-24): Hagerty's report of a leaked pre-production document also lists 0.32 for the C8, configuration not stated. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.
